limits.title: A claim to the formal of a body-less signature (interface method, call, construct or index signature, abstract method or setter) while the call is to another function
limits.note: The claimed destination emits no JavaScript and the call goes to another function. Controls: a call that does reach each signature is UNDECIDED type-only-declaration (judged correctly); the same call to a function with a body is CORRECT.

limits.title: A claim to a signature formal of an overloaded function that has one implementation
limits.note: Documented exception, not a defect of the grader: with one implementation either overload signature formal is WRONG implementation-slot and the implementation formal is CORRECT (oracle-032, oracle-037). A strict reading of the scope (a body-less signature emits nothing) would make both UNDECIDED; the exception is kept because a claim to a signature formal is a proved wrong slot. With no implementation both are UNDECIDED type-only-declaration.

limits.title: An import that reaches a value only through `export type *`, alone or forwarded by a named re-export
limits.note: The `export type *` mark sits on the export declaration, not on the symbol the alias walk reads, so the chain looks like a value. Controls: a live import is CORRECT; `import type` and an interface imported by name are UNDECIDED.

limits.title: Code a const enum, a folded enum initializer or a namespace holding only const enums erases
limits.note: TypeScript emits neither the namespace nor the read, or replaces the read with its constant. Controls: an instantiated namespace and a plain read of the same constant are CORRECT.

limits.title: A literal actual in a computed key that is erased (interface, type literal, ambient class, abstract method)
limits.note: The literal path skips the evaluated-context check. Control: the same call outside any erased key is CORRECT.

limits.title: `(id)<number>` and a bare `id<number>`: the value is read, the type arguments are not
limits.note: The role classifier takes the operand for a type position. Required verdict is CORRECT (a decided edge the oracle refuses or mislabels WRONG type-position). Control: `id(1)` is CORRECT.

limits.title: A same-line neighbour (a member read, another named function expression) suppresses a proved contradiction
limits.note: The neighbour check counts a token that cannot serve the claimed edge. Today UNDECIDED endpoint-coordinate-off; the stated rule requires the WRONG the control gets. Controls: the same programs with the neighbour on another line.

extra_controls.title: Controls the reviewers asked for
extra_controls.note: Import-equals `Alias -> void Alias` and a valid first-position `this` pseudo-parameter (`g(this: void, q)`) keep their CORRECT verdicts.
